title: Mira and Corvus's Star Picnic
markdown:
Mira the young witch lived in a cottage high in the Candlecap Mountains, where the air smelled of warm honey and pine needles. The thatched roof was a hug. Windows looked onto whispering trees. Corvus, her friendly crow, wore feathers like a midnight sky dusted with silver. His caws were not loud. They were hellos, good days. He perched on her shoulder, intelligent eyes cheerful.

One evening the sun painted rose and lavender. “Corvus, the stars are peeking, little shy eyes. Shall we have a gentle picnic? Through the Lantern Wood, where lanterns glow like sleepy fireflies, then a quiet spot on the mountain for supper under the sky-sparkles.”

He ruffled. Yes.

She packed a woven basket: blackberry scones still warm, chamomile tea that smelled like dreams, a woolen blanket the colour of warm oatmeal. Corvus tickled her ear. They set off, footsteps a soft patter on mossy stones.

The Lantern Wood was warm and glowing, just as Mira had imagined. Little lanterns strung from whispering branches cast a soft golden light. The whole wood felt like a secret cozy room. Night-blooming flowers drifted perfume like sleepy yawns. Mira hummed a melody as soft as falling leaves. Corvus hummed along with a low coo, a lovely rumble.

“It feels so peaceful here, Corvus. Like the whole world is taking a deep quiet breath.”

He nudged her cheek with his beak. She giggled, tiny silver bells.

As they ambled, the path opened into a small mossy clearing dappled with lantern light. There, hunched over a large scroll spread on a smooth grey stone, was a neat little goblin. Spectacles perched on his nose. A satchel burst with maps and drawing tools. Pipkin the goblin mapmaker, wonderfully detailed maps of the wood, brow furrowed with concentration.

“Oh dear. Did I put the Whispering Willow here, or a little further yonder? The light is just so. Shadows play tricks.”

“Hello there,” Mira said, lullaby-gentle. “Are you alright, little mapmaker?”

Twinkling eyes behind spectacles. “Hello, young witch. Hello, friendly crow. I am Pipkin. I am always so careful. I want the maps perfectly, precisely right. I worry I have drawn my favourite berry bush a tiny bit sideways.” An ink-stained finger: a bush that did look tilted.

Corvus hopped to a low branch, looked at map, at worried face, and cawed understanding.

Mira’s smile was a cozy fire. “Your maps are splendid. Neat, tidy, all the lovely details. Even if the berry bush is sideways on the page, the berries will still be plump and yummy wherever they are.”

Pipkin looked at the map, at Mira, at Corvus’s encouraging caw. A smile chased the worried lines. “Sideways berries. Still berries. And always the sweetest.” He rolled the map, relaxed. “You have made my mapping worries lighter, a breeze lifting a cloud.”

“Anytime. We are off for a mountain picnic under the stars. Join us for a moment? Warm blackberry scones.”

His eyes lit. “The most wonderful adventure.”

The three of them walked a little further through the gentle glow, footsteps light and happy. Soon they reached a wide flat clearing on the mountainside, the world stretching below like a sleepy blanket. The sky was a deep velvety blue, an ocean, sprinkled with a million winking stars like tiny diamonds on dark cloth, each shining its own gentle light.

Mira laid out the oatmeal blanket, a comforting contrast to the night. Pipkin produced a small sweet-smelling cake decorated with tiny edible flowers. Corvus, with a knowing look, found a plump juicy berry that had fallen from a nearby bush. They shared their simple supper in the quiet air. Crickets chirped like tiny musicians playing a sleepy tune. The breeze whispered like a mother singing a lullaby. Perfect shared contentment, a quiet pause in their gentle journeys.

After a while, as the stars twinkled brighter and a gentle tiredness settled like a warm quilt, Mira said, “It’s time to head home now, dear friends. The moon is starting its gentle climb, and our cozy cottage awaits.”

Pipkin nodded, spectacles gleaming in the starlight, a wise old owl of a goblin. “Thank you for the lovely company. I shall dream of perfectly plump sideways berries, and maps that are just right, in their own special way.”

Soft goodbyes, a promise of see-you-again hanging in the night. Mira and Corvus made their way down, hearts full and warm as a mug of hot cocoa. The Lantern Wood was quiet now, its glow a gentle memory, a sweet dream.

Back in the cottage, embers glowing softly in the hearth like sleeping little red eyes, Mira snuggled into her warm bed. Corvus settled into his nest on the windowsill, looking out at the vast star-filled sky, shiny feathers blending with the darkness. Everything was just right. The world outside peaceful and hushed; inside, safe and snug, filled with love and warmth. Soon, as gentle dreams swirled like fluffy clouds, Mira and Corvus drifted off to sleep, feeling very, very loved.
